```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(avesperu)
```

This vignette explains how `search_avesperu()` handles likely spelling variants in submitted scientific names. Start with a conservative threshold and review every non-exact match before using it in an analysis.

## Requirements

All examples use the local checklist bundled with `avesperu`; they do not call external services.

## Match a short list with spelling variants

```{r}
submitted <- c("Falco sparverius", "Tinamus osgodi", "Crypturellus sooui", "Penelope albipenis")
matches <- search_avesperu(submitted, max_distance = 0.05, return_details = TRUE)
matches[, c("name_submitted", "accepted_name", "dist")]
```

`dist` is the edit distance between a submitted value and its candidate. A value of zero denotes an exact match; values above zero require review.

## Choose a threshold

`max_distance` accepts either a proportion between zero and one or a nonnegative integer. A proportion scales with name length, while an integer sets an absolute number of character edits.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Exact matching only
search_avesperu(submitted, max_distance = 0, return_details = TRUE)

# Allow up to one character edit
search_avesperu(submitted, max_distance = 1, return_details = TRUE)

# Allow 10% of the name length
search_avesperu(submitted, max_distance = 0.1, return_details = TRUE)
```

## Escalate carefully

First identify names that remain unmatched, then retry only those rows using a documented threshold. Preserve the original submission and inspect each suggested match before updating source data.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
strict <- search_avesperu(submitted, max_distance = 0, return_details = TRUE)
unmatched <- strict$name_submitted[is.na(strict$accepted_name)]
retry <- search_avesperu(unmatched, max_distance = 0.1, return_details = TRUE)
```
